title: Replication Event ID Recognition
summary: Single-select: identify which Event ID indicates a topology mismatch.
question: Which Directory Service event ID indicates that AD's replication topology configuration doesn't match the network's actual physical topology?
explanation: Event ID 1311 (NTDS KCC) specifically indicates the replication configuration information doesn't accurately reflect the physical network topology. 2042 is tombstone lifetime exceeded, 2087 is DNS resolution success-with-warning, 1988 is a lingering object reference.

title: Replication Troubleshooting Order
summary: Single-select: correct order of first checks after ruling out intentional disruption/hardware failure.
question: After ruling out intentional disconnection and hardware failure, which root cause does Microsoft's troubleshooting guidance list FIRST to check?
explanation: The documented checklist orders root causes as: network connectivity, name resolution (DNS), replication topology, authentication and authorization, then the directory database store and replication engine/scheduling.

title: Forest-Wide FSMO Roles
summary: Multi-select: identify the two forest-wide FSMO roles.
question: Select the TWO FSMO roles that exist once per forest rather than once per domain.
explanation: Schema Master and Domain Naming Master are forest-wide (one per forest). PDC Emulator, RID Master, and Infrastructure Master exist once per domain.

title: Transfer vs Seize
summary: Single-select scenario: correct action when the current role holder is still online.
question: The DC holding the Infrastructure Master role is being decommissioned as part of a planned migration and is currently healthy and online. What is the correct action?
options: Transfer the role to another DC
Seize the role on another DC
Leave the role in place until the DC is powered off, then seize it
Delete the role from AD DS
correct_answer: Transfer the role to another DC
explanation: Transfer (not seize) is correct whenever the current role holder is online and available; seizing should be reserved for when the current holder is permanently unavailable, since a seized-then-recovered original holder creates a dangerous dual-role-holder condition.

title: Forest Recovery Data Loss
summary: Single-select: what is unavoidably lost in a forest recovery.
question: A forest is recovered from a trusted backup taken 3 days before the failure. What is unavoidably lost as a result?
options: All objects and updates made in the 3 days since that backup
Only the schema partition changes made in the last 3 days
Nothing, as long as SYSVOL is restored authoritatively
Only computer account passwords changed in the last 3 days
correct_answer: All objects and updates made in the 3 days since that backup
explanation: Forest recovery restores each domain to its state at the time of the last trusted backup: all objects added since, all updates to existing objects since, and any schema/configuration partition changes since are lost - not just one category of change.

title: First-DC Recovery Order
summary: Single-select: which domain's DC is restored first.
question: In a multi-domain forest recovery, which domain's DC must be restored first?
options: The domain with the most users
The domain with the most recent backup
Whichever domain's DCs are physically closest to the recovery team
explanation: The forest root domain is recovered first because it stores the Schema Admins and Enterprise Admins groups, maintains the trust hierarchy, and typically holds the forest DNS root - other domains are recovered afterward, parent before child.

title: Kerberos Error Meaning
question: A client's Security event log records error KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW. What does this indicate?
options: The client and target server clocks are out of sync
A duplicate SPN exists on two accounts
correct_answer: The client and target server clocks are out of sync
explanation: KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW specifically means the client and target server clocks are out of sync beyond Kerberos's tolerance; the fix is time synchronization (e.g. w32tm /resync), not an SPN or DC-availability fix.

title: Delegation Type for Cross-Forest Access
summary: Single-select: which delegation type supports cross-forest scenarios.
question: Which Kerberos delegation type is supported when the front-end and back-end services reside in different, trusted forests?
options: None - cross-forest delegation is never supported
explanation: Per Microsoft's delegation topology table, constrained delegation is not supported across different forests, while RBCD is supported (marked with a caveat that the front-end service account must be able to authenticate across the trust). Unconstrained delegation is also technically supported cross-forest but explicitly 'not recommended' due to its broad blast radius.

title: gMSA Minimum Domain Functional Level
summary: Single-select: minimum domain functional level for gMSA.
question: What is the minimum domain functional level required to use group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA)?
options: There is no minimum - gMSA works on any domain functional level
explanation: gMSAs require domain functional level Windows Server 2012 or later; they are not applicable to domains below that level. The earlier standalone MSA (sMSA) was introduced with Windows Server 2008 R2, but that is a different, single-server-only feature.

title: gMSA and Failover Clustering
summary: Single-select: does the Cluster service itself support gMSA directly.
question: Does the Windows failover Cluster service itself support using a gMSA directly?
options: No, but services running on top of the Cluster service can still use one if they natively support gMSA/sMSA
No, gMSA can never be used anywhere near a failover cluster
Yes, but only on Windows Server 2012
correct_answer: No, but services running on top of the Cluster service can still use one if they natively support gMSA/sMSA
explanation: Microsoft's documentation is explicit that failover clusters don't support gMSAs directly at the Cluster service level, but a Windows service, an app pool, or a scheduled task running on top of the Cluster service can still use a gMSA or sMSA if it natively supports one.
